newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foster's sees great growth potential.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foster's sees great growth potential.

text.p: Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said on Monday it saw great growth prospects for its domestic brewing and wine businesses and predicted a substantial profit increase for recently acquired winemaker Mildara Blass.
"We have a very solid earnings base and great growth prospects, particularly from CUB (Carlton & United Breweries) and Mildara Blass," chief executive Ted Kunkel told reporters.
Commenting on a better than expected net profit of A$293 million for 1995/96, Kunkel said he expected Mildara's earnings before interest and tax to increase substantially over the next five years.

"That will be done without the need for further acquisitions," Kunkel added. He described Molson's weak result as an abberation and predicted the Canadian brewer's contribution to group profit would increase as the benefits of its restructuring began to flow through.

Molson Breweries posted a 55 percent slump in net profit for the year to April 1 after writing off restructuring costs. Molson contributed A$61 million to Foster's profit, down from A$72 million in 1994/95.
"Costs have been reduced significantly and this will help our profitability in the future," he said of Molson result.

Foster's two percent rise in net profit to A$293.3 million for the year to June 30 exceeded the average market forecast for a pre-abnormal net profit of around A$270 million, and confirmed the group's local brewer as its growth engine.
Carlton and United Breweries' earnings before interest and tax leapt 16 percent to A$327 million on increased market share and growth from its pubs and leisure business.
The performance of Foster's offshore operations were in stark contrast with its surge in local earnings, which included A$16 million EBIT from newly acquired wine-maker Mildara Blass.
Foster's shares were down a cent at A$2.30 by 3.45 a.m. (0545 GMT).
